subject: Architecture
title: Brutalism: Concrete and Controversy
description: A 60-second lesson on Brutalism: Concrete and Controversy.

hook.text: Brutalist buildings are raw concrete, massive, and divisive — people either love them or loathe them.

buildup.text: The name comes from 'béton brut,' French for raw concrete — not from 'brutal.'

discovery.text: Post-war governments chose Brutalism because concrete was cheap and expressed social equality.

twist.text: Decades of neglect turned many Brutalist buildings into stained, leaking eyesores that people hated.

climax.text: A new generation now fights to save Brutalist landmarks, calling them honest and powerful.

punchline.text: Hated, neglected, and now Instagram-famous. Concrete endures.

quiz.question: Where does the name 'Brutalism' actually come from?
options: The English word 'brutal' describing its appearance
A German architect named Bruno Brutalis
